title: The 10 Best Multi-Tools
subtitle: Pliers multi-tools from Leatherman, Gerber, SOG and budget brands, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A multi-tool folds pliers, a knife, screwdrivers and more into one pocket-size tool. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Leatherman, Gerber, SOG and value brands on rating, review volume and features (a long warranty, locking tools, one-hand opening and a sheath). Many make good gifts under $50 for anyone who fixes things.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: 14-In-1 Multitool with Safety Locking, Professional Stainless Steel Multitool Pliers Pocket Knife, Bottle Opener, Screwdriver with Nylon Sheath
avoid.flag: Padded tool count; placeholder part number
avoid.verdict: A basic pliers multi-tool whose '14-in-1' count is padded and whose listing data is placeholder text. For about $20 more, the Gerber Suspension NXT has a known brand and 23,830 reviews behind it.
reasons: The 14 functions count the pliers head three times (long nose, round nose and cutting pliers) and list three sizes of flat screwdriver separately.
The manufacturer part number is 'abc-001' and the manufacturer field names a different company (TSKECN) than the brand, so tracing who makes it is hard.
The listing gives two different sizes for the same tool: 3.9 x 1.6 x 0.6 inches and a folded size of 4.7 x 1.96 x 1.18.

buyers_guide.q: Which multi-tool should I start with?
buyers_guide.a: For most people, a full-size pliers tool like the Leatherman Wingman or Wave+ or the Gerber Suspension NXT. If you only want something on your keys, the Gerber Dime. If you mostly need a knife, the Skeletool CX.

Less than you'd think. Many budget tools count each pliers function and each screwdriver size separately to reach 20+. Check the tools you'll actually use: pliers, a knife, flat and Phillips drivers, and scissors.
Leatherman backs its tools with a 25-year warranty and makes the Wave+, Wingman and Skeletool in Portland, Oregon. The steel, fit and finish are better than budget tools.
Yes. A lock stops a blade or screwdriver folding onto your fingers when you push. Most tools here lock; check before you buy.

buyers_guide.q: Can I carry one on a plane?
buyers_guide.a: Not in carry-on luggage in the US if it has a knife blade. Pack it in checked luggage.
